### ELEVATION AND ARCHITECTURAL DETAILS OF THE TEMPLE OF NEPTUNE

<note>This engraving illustrates the front facade and a detailed profile of the temple's architectural components, likely the same Temple of Neptune discussed on the preceding pages.</note>

This plate presents a detailed **elevation** <term>a scale drawing of the side of a building</term> and a corresponding **cross-section** of the temple's facade. On the right side of the illustration, the temple's front is shown with three **Corinthian columns** <note>The most ornate of the three classical Greek orders, characterized by capitals decorated with acanthus leaves.</note>. These columns are fluted and support a massive **entablature** and **pediment**. 

The **pediment** <term>the triangular gable forming the roof's end</term> is decorated with classical statuary. A figure on the left is depicted holding a staff and a branch, while a second statue rests upon the far right corner. Behind the elegant columns, the interior wall is represented with detailed brickwork, suggesting the structural reality of the building.

On the left side of the engraving, the architect has provided a technical **profile** or cross-section of the moldings and cornices. This allows for a precise understanding of the decorative "projections" that would not be visible from a flat front view. 

**Table of Technical Measurements**
<note>Measurements are indicated by various letters corresponding to specific points on the drawing. The primary unit of measure is the <term>Piede</term> (Foot), abbreviated as 'P'.</note>

| Label | Architectural Element | Measurement / Note |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **A** | Column Base | Found at the bottom of the fluted shaft. |
| **B** | Corinthian Capital | The ornate top of the column. |
| **C** | Entablature | The horizontal section resting on the capitals. |
| **D** | Cornice Profile | Detailed cross-section shown on the left. |
| **P 38** | Column Height | Measured at 38 feet. |
| **P I L** | Section Width | Marked on the left-hand profile. |
| **G** | Scale Bar | <note>original: "G"; used to calculate the proportions of the various elements.</note> |

The **stylobate** <term>the continuous base or platform supporting a row of columns</term> features circular decorative elements and specific fractional measurements, such as **P S G 3/4**, detailing the exact proportions of the temple's foundation.

### ELEVATION AND ARCHITECTURAL DETAILS OF THE TEMPLE OF NEPTUNE

<note>This plate serves as a technical companion to the text, providing the "grammar" of the building's classical components.</note>

This engraving illustrates the detailed **elevation** <term>a scale drawing of the side of a building</term> and the corresponding **profiles** <term>cross-section drawings showing the contours of moldings</term> of the temple. 

On the left side of the plate, we see a partial view of the facade. A decorative **pediment** <term>the triangular gable above the columns</term> crowns the structure, featuring a sculpted figure standing at its peak. The facade is supported by a series of fluted columns topped with **Corinthian capitals** <note>These are the most ornate style of ancient capitals, distinguished by their carved acanthus leaves and scrolls.</note>. Behind this elegant colonnade, the architect has rendered the interior wall with a brickwork pattern to indicate the structural masonry.

The right side of the plate provides a high-magnification view of the specific moldings that make up the temple's base and its upper crowning elements. By providing these profiles, the architect ensures that builders can replicate the exact "projection" and "recession" of the stone carvings, which create the play of light and shadow characteristic of classical architecture.

**Table of Technical Proportions**
<note>Measurements are given in <term>Feet</term> (original: P for *Piedi* or *Palmi*). Numbers without a 'P' refer to smaller subdivisions or units of proportion used by the architect.</note>

| Label | Architectural Element | Dimension / Measurement |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **A** | Profile of the Column Base | 44 units high |
| **E** | Width of the Fluted Column Shaft | 3 <term>Feet</term> |
| **B / F** | Specific points on the Facade Elevation | <note>Used for correlating the front view with the profile view.</note> |
| — | Total Height of the Column Shaft | 38 <term>Feet</term> |
| — | Width of the Temple Base/Plinth | 67 1/2 and 63 1/4 <term>Feet</term> |
| — | Height of the Entablature | 21 <term>Feet</term> and 10 units |

The **frieze** <note>the middle part of the entablature above the columns</note> depicted in the upper right profile is adorned with a delicate scroll or foliage pattern, a hallmark of the Corinthian order's decorative richness. The various numbers—such as 21, 17 1/2, and 23—marked along the base (**A**) indicate the precise thickness of each molding, ensuring that the finished temple would possess the perfect mathematical harmony intended by the ancients.

->### FOURTH BOOK<-
<note>original: "OLTI BRO", a fragment of "QUARTO LIBRO" (Fourth Book), likely split across the header of the two-page spread.</note>

**Technical Plate of the Entablature**

This engraving provides a meticulous architectural study of the upper structure of the temple, focusing on the **entablature** <term>the ensemble of moldings and bands that lie horizontally above the columns</term>. The plate is designed as a manual for architects, using a numerical system to define the perfect proportions of the Corinthian order.

The structure is divided into three distinct sections:

*   **The Cornice:** The highest section, featuring projecting elements such as **dentils** <term>small, tooth-like blocks</term> and decorative moldings designed to cast clear, geometric shadows.
*   **The Frieze:** The central decorative section. It is embellished with a rich, continuous relief of **foliage and mythical creatures** <note>The figures shown are griffins, ancient symbols of strength and protection, often associated with the god Apollo but also used in grand public architecture to signify majesty.</note>.
*   **The Architrave:** The lowest part of the entablature, resting directly on the columns. It is divided into several **fascias** <term>flat, horizontal strips or bands</term>, which provide a sense of layered stability.

**Proportional Measurements**
<note>The numbers on the plate indicate the "minutes" or units of proportion. These allow the design to be scaled to any size while maintaining the exact visual harmony intended by the original Roman architects. The mark "P1" refers to 1 Foot (original: *Palmo* or *Piede*).</note>

| Architectural Component | Proportional Values and Measurements |
| :--- | :--- |
| **Cornice & Upper Moldings** | 22, 24, 27, 12½, 13, 2, 8, 27, 24 |
| **Decorative Frieze** | 17, 12½, 15, 7, 17, 2, 15 |
| **Architrave & Fascias** | 6, 9, 3, 6, 20, 25, 5, 21, 24, 7, 2 |
| **Base Profiles & Projections** | 6, 7, 9, 12, 2, 7, 24, 25, 26, 27, 20, 13, 15 |
| **Scale Reference** | 1 Foot (P1), 34 units |

The layout allows a builder to see both the front-facing decoration and the **profile** <term>the side view showing how far the stone carvings project</term> simultaneously. This ensures that the depth of the carvings—essential for the play of light in classical architecture—is as accurate as the height.

**Architectural Detail Plate**

This plate illustrates the highly refined decorative elements of the temple’s interior and exterior. These drawings served as a "pattern book" for Renaissance architects to recreate the grandeur of Roman antiquity.

### Decorative Panels and Ceiling
The upper portion of the plate displays various ornamental designs:

*   **Panel H:** A detail of an arched decorative panel. It features **grotesque motifs** <term>a style of Roman ornament involving intertwined foliage, human figures, and mythical creatures</term> and elaborate scrollwork.
*   **The Coffered Ceiling:** To the right is a large rectangular panel showing a **lacunar** <term>a recessed ceiling panel or coffer</term>. It is decorated with a central rosette and surrounded by a **cyma** <term>an S-shaped molding</term> carved with floral patterns.

The lower section provides the exact measurements for the moldings of the pedestals and bases.

**Pedestal Profile G**
<margin>Part 2, Unit 7</margin>
<note>original: "P. 2. G. 7." Palladio uses a system of "Parts" (P.) and "Units" or "Minutes" (G. for *gradi* or *minuti*) to define proportions regardless of the actual size of the building.</note>
This profile shows a corner molding. The annotations <gloss>round</gloss> <note>original: "oldo" and "ondo", fragments of *rotondo* or *tondino*</note> indicate the curved nature of the **bead molding** <term>a small, convex molding with a semi-circular cross-section</term>.

The numbers 1 through 26 scattered across the profiles indicate specific measurement points used to determine the projection and height of each individual curve and flat surface.
